name: Hiwa Feizi
title: Data Engineer
summary:
Data engineer at Allianz Netherlands. I take the lead when the work needs it: as client-side technical authority, I evaluated and accepted the work of a 10+ person IBM delivery team on a SAS-to-Snowflake migration.

My default is to automate; what I can't automate, I use AI to make more efficient. I'll do the quick fix when it's needed, but then I look for the pattern that makes it unnecessary next time: validation at 50M rows a day, programmatic generation of 2,000+ models, repo-wide cleanup that retired 5,000 dead tables, 8-hour onboarding tasks turned into minutes. Each one a one-off problem that became something the team reuses.

I bring a software engineer's and an AI engineer's mentality to data engineering: structure, code design, validation. It's a diverse skill set I use daily, and it makes me fast enough that scope keeps finding me, at work and in side projects like a learned racing bot that reached the world's top 0.2%.

bullets.text: Client-side technical authority for the SAS-to-Snowflake migration: evaluated and accepted the work of a 10+ person IBM delivery team (design review, acceptance criteria, dbt code review) and first point of escalation for IBM-side issues. Drove validation and data-movement design changes IBM adopted.
Defined the SAS team's migration tasks and trained them on dbt/Snowflake as needed, enabling parity validation independently from the SAS side.
Defined the source-loading strategy and co-designed new ingestion processes with IT for sources never loaded before, including mainframe extracts in packed-decimal format.
Crawled the SAS server to extract transformation logic from 1,000+ legacy files, cataloguing reusable code that accelerated conversion of legacy pipelines to dbt.
On pstag, the Data Office's upstream source: reviewed PRs, set the team's PR standards, and validated results against data; evaluated enhancement ideas and proposed my own.
Migrated pstag from script-based logic to dbt: programmatically generated ~660 YAML configs and 2,000+ SQL models from Snowflake metadata.
Built the validation framework (dbt macros plus runtime checks) proving 100% row- and column-level parity against production on daily loads exceeding 50 million rows.

Built cleanup tooling over the repo and dbt manifest lineage: removed ~5,000 idle tables, flagged 2,000 more that are unreferenced anywhere in the repo for team investigation, and identified 400 models no longer consumed by the user layer.

Restructured the staging layer (2,000+ models across 50+ schedules) and its tagging system end to end; when a downstream cross-team break surfaced, traced it to the IT side, requested the code change, and had every issue resolved by 9am with stakeholders notified at each step.

Built a generic Python parser for the mainframe PD binary format after spotting silent data loss in the prior CSV ingestion: binary in, CSV out, batched and logged, with per-table config in version-controlled JSON so changes ship through PRs instead of IT tickets.
Built an API over Azure Blob Storage that streams and analyzes 20+ GB files in place, turning cross-table data-quality reports into a seconds-long operation and pushing fixes upstream to the source.
Automated recurring platform work against the Snowflake API: zero-copy clones per source schema, parallel test and data extraction, and threaded processing with structured logging.
Built an automated documentation system extracting raw-level metadata from multi-format, multi-language source files into table-based documentation in three languages.
Co-designed the team's reusable dbt macro library for table and view generation, and operate dbt Cloud as the orchestration layer: scheduled jobs, CI/CD, and production deployments.

groups.heading: AI enablement across the Data Office

bullets.text: Built an AI-driven SAS↔Snowflake column-matching pipeline chaining LLM calls with live connections to both systems, sampling row-level values and validating matches programmatically, reaching 93% average accuracy; it became the team's standard for validating the migration and reviewing dbt developers' PRs.

Built a context-locked AI workflow for onboarding new sources: tasks estimated at 8 hours now take 5 minutes of AI work plus 5 to 55 minutes of validation, with predefined deliverables identical run to run, debuggable by engineers with no prior pipeline knowledge.

Introduced Claude Code to the Data Office and wrote the repo-level guide files that standardize how it's used: plan-before-code and review conventions baked into the repo context, working for every engineer who touches the codebase.
Helped peer technical leads on other teams build their own agents on Allianz's internal AI platform and adopt the Snowflake-API automation patterns.
Proposed and implemented a new processing architecture cutting end-to-end pipeline runtime ~99%: from ~1.5 days to minutes.
Rebuilt undocumented Oracle SQL pipelines into dbt models on Snowflake at >=99.9% data accuracy, with ~70% of tables reaching full parity across millions of rows.
Simplified the architecture by removing redundant processing steps, cutting compute cost and maintenance overhead.
Built a Power BI dashboard monitoring dbt Cloud runs with hierarchical filtering and enriched metadata.

Built an AI-assisted recruitment platform solo, end to end: Flask/PostgreSQL backend, recruiter dashboards with role-based access, and OpenAI-driven job-description generation for Dutch businesses running without full HR systems.

Ran it as a production system on GCP: containerized Cloud Run services, Cloud Build CI/CD, Cloud Storage for applicant resumes, and structured logging, the same deploy discipline I'd expect at work, applied to my own product.
Killed it deliberately in Dec 2025 and shut the company down properly, KVK deregistration included. The full reasoning is in the post-mortem.

Built an automation platform that generates and publishes LinkedIn content end to end: LinkedIn API integration, OpenAI text generation, and scheduled publishing behind user accounts with secure session management.
Designed the orchestration layer to run without daily attention: Cloud Functions and Cloud Tasks running scheduled content creation and background jobs, deployed as containerized services with CI/CD.
Retired it after a year; its Cloud Tasks orchestration pattern became the direct ancestor of the Meme Factory pipeline's self-scheduling task loader.

projects.name: Mad Pod Racing - A Learned Game Bot in the World Top 500

bullets.text: Reached 459th of 233,508 on CodinGame's Mad Pod Racing world leaderboard with a learned bot: PPO self-play, DAgger imitation, and league evolution.
Rebuilt the game physics as a GPU-vectorized PyTorch simulator averaging 600 games per second on one consumer RTX 4060: the throughput behind all 29 experiments.
Iterated the reward function against turn-by-turn visualizations of games and reward signals, raising the win rate against the fixed hand-coded benchmark bot from 18% to 100%.
Built a dedicated defender bootcamp with adversarial spawns and urgency-weighted rewards, turning near-certain breaches into full-lap holds.
Kept networks tiny and training short by engineering the inputs (calculated features in, noise excluded) instead of hoping a bigger net would sort it out.
Shipped the whole system (nets, weights, geometry) as one self-contained Python file with embedded weights trimmed to fit CodinGame's submission limit.

projects.name: LinkedIn Meme Factory - Automated Content Pipeline

bullets.text: Built a Python pipeline that generates niche-specific LinkedIn meme content with Grok, validates each batch through a second LLM pass against a per-template humor model in a 1,000-line catalog, and renders 20 PIL meme templates.

Designed two execution modes sharing one codebase: eager pre-rendering with direct Cloud Tasks scheduling, and lazy on-demand rendering inside a GCP Cloud Function, driven by a self-perpetuating task loader that queues a day of Cloud Tasks and then schedules itself for tomorrow.

Ran it fully autonomously across 3 LinkedIn business pages for a pre-registered 100-day window, posting twice a day. Total Grok cost: $0.34. Engagement was effectively zero; the 10-niche fan-out the architecture was built for was blocked by LinkedIn's business-page limits. Wrote the post-mortem with full cost data anyway.

projects.name: Half Stupid - Teaching Minecraft Agents to Survive From Scratch

bullets.text: Built a dual-timescale neural network (reflex layer at every tick, context layer every 5 ticks) using shared learned embeddings across 2048 block/item/entity types, processing 557 raw inputs into 23 actions with zero human-labeled knowledge.

Trained with vanilla REINFORCE on a survival-only reward (+1 alive, -10,000 on death) and got emergent food-seeking, distinct agent personalities, and inter-agent social dynamics without any reward shaping.
Closed the project on evidence: profiled the Minecraft/Malmo substrate to a hard 4-agent, ~4,000 ticks/sec ceiling, quantified that further training was compute-starved, and stopped there.

projects.name: Thesis - Predicting Perceptions of Dutch Company Names

bullets.text: Built an end-to-end pipeline predicting human trait judgments (femininity, evilness, trustworthiness, smartness) from Dutch brand-like names, aggregating Bayesian posterior samples from raw ranking experiments into stable regression targets.
Engineered three feature pipelines: character-level unigrams (27D), padded bigrams (479D), and contextual RobBERT embeddings (768D).
Trained and evaluated 64+ models (Elastic Net and feedforward networks) across in-domain, out-of-domain, and few-shot splits with fixed seeds and consistent R² evaluation.
Multimodal speech recognition with AV-HuBERT: built the lip-extraction and audio-video alignment pipeline and a parallelized inference setup processing 21,000+ audio/video files.
PetMatters: led a team of 8 building a multi-service AI application; trained and integrated T5 models for English-to-Dutch translation and form-driven content generation.
Battle-C: modular C++ game engine with AI opponent logic and real-time state tracking.
Wildfire-risk prediction: LightGBM pipeline modeling fire outbreak risk from environmental data.
